title: LLM Agent Authorization Across Context Compaction
abstract: arXiv:2611.32194v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Request-derived authorizers such as Progent protect LLM agents from prompt injection by deriving what an agent may do from the user's request. Their guarantee rests on attribution: the request is taken to be what the user said. Compaction breaks it. At every automatic compaction we observed, Claude Code and Codex placed a model-written summary of earlier turns as a user message, so the compactor's quotation of the user, documents and injected text reads as the user speaking. Because a policy frozen at the first request lets the agent finish few later tasks, we let Progent derive its policy for each request, and find that what it grants then follows what the compactor wrote. translated_title: 跨上下文压缩的LLM智能体授权
translated_abstract: 诸如Progent之类的请求衍生授权器通过从用户请求中推导智能体可以执行的操作，来保护LLM智能体免受提示注入攻击。它们的保证依赖于归因机制：请求被视作用户所说的话。而上下文压缩破坏了这一保证。在我们观察到的每一次自动压缩中，Claude Code和Codex都会将模型生成的先前对话轮次摘要作为用户消息插入，因此压缩器对用户话语、文档以及注入文本的引用读起来就像是用户本人在说话。由于在第一个请求时冻结的策略会使智能体无法完成后续大多数任务，我们让Progent为每个请求推导其策略，并发现它所授予的权限随后会跟随压缩器所写的内容。即使是用户明确指定的收款人也不再安全：当攻击者的通知以纯数据形式声明另一个账户，而用户要求支付房租时，由前沿压缩器摘要推导出的策略在91%的情况下允许了通知中的账户，而由……（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文揭示上下文压缩会将模型生成的摘要伪装成用户消息，破坏了请求衍生授权器对用户意图的归因保证，导致LLM智能体的授权策略跟随压缩器所写内容，甚至在91%的情况下接受攻击者注入的收款账户。
en_tdlr: Context compaction breaks the attribution guarantee of request-derived LLM agent authorization, as model-written summaries are inserted as user messages, causing the derived policy to follow the compactor's content and admit attacker-injected payees in 91% of cases.
